interest: Shows FBI surveillance of the Portland Japanese consulate's 1941 asset survey, file destruction, and a Nisei citizenship renunciation form.
overview: August 1941 Hoover letter to Berle reports the Portland Japanese consulate surveyed Issei assets (over $2.18 million), and that Acting Consul Oka burned confidential files and moved codebooks after the Cabinet's fall; encloses a Nisei form for renouncing Japanese citizenship.

people.name: H. Y. Kato
people.role: Resident of Oregon listed as the wealthiest Japanese in the state

subfiles.about: FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover reports confidential intelligence on the Portland Japanese Consulate's survey of Issei assets, destruction of confidential records, and emergency security measures.
subfiles.summary: Hoover tells Berle the Portland Japanese consulate surveyed Oregon Issei, reporting $2,187,920 in assets for Tokyo; after the Cabinet's resignation, Acting Consul Oka burned confidential files and moved the codebook to his home amid heightened espionage concerns.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. E. Hoover to Adolf A. Berle, Jr., Regarding Japanese Consulate Activities in Portland, Oregon

subfiles.about: English translation of a standard Japanese administrative form for renouncing Japanese citizenship under the Law of Nationality.
subfiles.summary: Translated Japanese form for Nisei to renounce citizenship under the Law of Nationality, with fields for family and residence details.
subfiles.title: Enclosure: Translation of Japanese Petition to Renounce Citizenship
